context:
The script is the single source of truth for bounds health. It has two
modes:
  1. `--fail-on=ceiling-minus-one` (blocking, offline): parses
     pyproject.toml, reads uv.lock, fails if any capped dep's locked
     major equals `cap_major - 1`. This is the "must decide before ship"
     signal.
  2. `--report-only` (non-blocking, online): fetches upstream changelogs
     (PyPI + GitHub releases API with auth token) for each capped dep
     between locked and cap; greps for breaking-change keywords
     ("BREAKING", "removed", "deprecated API"); emits a markdown summary
     suitable for appending to release-notes-draft.md.

Quarterly review and release-time gate share the same script so the
check logic doesn't drift between the two entry points.
description:
Quality plan follow-up. `quality-add-dependency-upper-bounds-policy`
added caps to sqlglot<31, click<9, pydantic<3, pyarrow<24, duckdb<2
with rationale comments in pyproject.toml. Those caps are enforced by
`uv lock` at install time, but nothing today blocks a release if:
  - a capped dep has drifted close to its ceiling (locked at ceiling-1
    minor - forces a bump/hold decision the moment upstream ships the
    next major)
  - the cap is silently masking a stale pin (the locked version has
    been frozen for many minors while the upstream has moved on)
  - an upstream major has landed that would require re-validation
    before bumping the cap

Add a release-time gate so the bounds policy actively guides shipping
rather than just sitting in the manifest.

anti_patterns.why: changelogs are noisy and keyword-based grep will false-positive

anti_patterns.dont: hard-code the capped dep list in the script
anti_patterns.why: that duplicates pyproject.toml and will drift

anti_patterns.dont: require network for the blocking gate
anti_patterns.why: CI will page on upstream outages

anti_patterns.dont: silently skip on lockfile parse failures
anti_patterns.instead: fail hard with a clear error
anti_patterns.why: that turns the gate into theater

preserves.behavior: Bounds policy unchanged: cap only high-risk deps, document rationale inline
Fast test suite green after the script and its tests land
Release workflow still succeeds for the current lockfile (no retroactive failures at merge time)
Script is idempotent and offline-capable for the ceiling-minus-one check; only changelog-diff mode requires network

scope_rules.path_glob: pyproject.toml caps (use as-is; bump is a separate decision)
uv.lock (the gate reads it; does not write it)

verifications.description: Script runs clean against current lockfile
verifications.expected: exit 0; report shows all caps green OR one entry in ceiling-minus-one warning
markdown table listing each capped dep, locked version, cap, changelog link

verifications.description: Release workflow lints clean after integration

work_units.summary: Write scripts/check_dependency_bounds.py: parse capped deps from pyproject.toml, run `uv lock --upgrade --dry-run`, emit structured report (capped dep, locked version, cap, next-major availability)
Implement `--fail-on=ceiling-minus-one` mode: exit non-zero if any locked version equals ceiling minus one (e.g., sqlglot 30.x with cap <31). Forces explicit bump/hold decision before ship.
Implement `--report-only` mode: for each capped dep, fetch upstream changelog between locked and ceiling; surface breaking-change keywords into release-notes draft artifact (markdown).
Wire into .github/workflows/release.yml as a required job before tag/publish. Uses `--fail-on=ceiling-minus-one` for the blocking step and `--report-only` for the release-notes surfacing.
Update review-dependency-upper-bounds-quarterly.yaml to invoke the same script for the quarterly review - single source of truth for bounds health.
Document the gate and its recovery paths in AGENTS.md 'Dependency Upper Bounds' section (how to bump a cap, how to override in emergencies, links to the script).
